newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees 1997 world wheat crop at 585 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees 1997 world wheat crop at 585 mln tonnes.

text.p: World wheat production in 1997 will be 585 million tonnes, according to estimates released by the International Grains Council on Thursday.
The previous IGC estimate, made in November, was 580 million tonnes and its figure for 1996 is also 580 million.
In its latest market report, the IGC forecasts rises from last year in the EU, central and eastern Europe, Russia and Ukraine.
It predicts falls in Argentina, Canada and Australia.
EU wheat area is forecast to rise as a result of a cut in set-aside.
Even though average yields may not match those of 1996, the EU crop could reach 100.6 million tonnes, compared with 99.4 million in 1996.
In central and eastern Europe the IGC predicts a recovery after a poor performance in 1996. The region's 1997 production is put at 32.4 million tonnes, compared with 1996's 26.2 million.
Russian production is seen rising to 36.0 million tonnes, from 34.9 million. Ukraine wheat production is seen at 17.0 million tonnes, compared with the 1996 estimate of 13.4 million.

Argentina's production is seen down at 13.0 million tonnes, compared with an exceptional crop of 15.5 million in 1996. Canada's crop is also forecast down from a bumper 1996 harvest. The IGC sees the 1997 crop at 28.0 million tonnes, compared with 30.5 million in 1996.
Australia is also seen falling short of a bumper 1996 crop, with 1997 output seen at 17.5 million tonnes, compared with 1996's 23.0 million. But the level is still above 1995's 17.0 million.
